historical_claims.anchor: It claims that for real subspaces whose principal angles are all at most sixty degrees, the direct rotation minimizes every unitarily invariant norm of the full displacement.
Davis and Kahan also give two examples showing that the unsquared statement fails in general.

Bolotnikov, Li, and Rodman, in 2001, studied minimal distortion problems for unitary maps carrying one subspace onto another, proved Q-norm optimality, and gave counterexamples for Schatten norms with exponent between one and two.

Qiu, Zhang, and Li later repeated the sixty-degree assertion, and Zhang and Qiu noted in 2010 that trace-norm minimality fails in general, without addressing the particular real, small-angle restriction.
As far as the journal paper's authors could determine, the contradiction of the printed real claim at every positive angle had not previously been made explicit.
